title: Advancing Supply Chain Planning: SAP Named a Leader in Multiple 2026 IDC MarketScape Assessments
summary: SAP was named a Leader in multiple 2026 IDC MarketScape assessments for supply chain planning across key industries. Read to learn more.
body_markdown:
[SAP](https://www.sap.com/products/scm/supply-chain-planning.html) has been named a Leader in the[2026 IDC MarketScape for Worldwide Supply Chain Planning Overall Vendor Assessment](https://www.sap.com/documents/1365789) *. We believe this recognition comes at an important moment for supply chain leaders, as persistent disruption, changing demand, and rapid advances in AI make the connection between planning and execution more critical than ever.


Supply chain decisions do not happen in isolation. A change in demand can affect inventory, production, suppliers, logistics, and financial outcomes. The faster conditions change, the more important it becomes to connect those decisions and give people the context they need to act.


That is why we are proud of SAP’s recognition across the new IDC MarketScape assessments for supply chain planning.


*IDC MarketScape vendor analysis model is designed to provide an overview of the competitive fitness of technology and suppliers in a given market. The research methodology utilizes a rigorous scoring methodology based on both qualitative and quantitative criteria that results in a single graphical illustration of each supplier’s position within a given market. The Capabilities score measures supplier product, go-to-market and business execution in the short-term. The Strategy score measures alignment of supplier strategies with customer requirements in a 3-5 year timeframe. Supplier market share is represented by the size of the icons.*


In addition to the Overall Supply Chain Planning assessment, SAP has been named a Leader in the assessments for Process Industries**, Life Sciences***, Discrete Industries†, and Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG)††. SAP was also named a Major Player in the assessment for Distribution Industries†††.


For us, the breadth of this recognition is meaningful. We believe it reflects the importance of connecting planning to the industry-specific processes, data, and decisions that ultimately determine how well a supply chain responds.


## **Planning has to understand the business**


Every industry plans differently because every industry operates differently. Life sciences companies need to account for factors such as batches, shelf life, and clinical supply. Discrete manufacturers manage complex bills of material, product configurations, and constrained capacity. CPG companies need to synchronize demand, production, packaging, inventory, and deployment.


Enhance decision-making across the supply chain using an AI-enabled planning platform


[Learn more](https://www.sap.com/products/scm/supply-chain-planning.html)


That business context matters even more as AI becomes part of everyday supply chain decision-making. AI can help planners identify patterns, simulate scenarios, and automate individual tasks—learn more in our[AI Buyers’ Guide to Intelligent, Decision-Centric Planning](https://www.sap.com/products/scm/supply-chain-planning.html?pdf-asset=cc32721f-637f-0010-bca6-c68f7e60039b&page=1) . But isolated intelligence produces isolated value. The bigger opportunity is to apply AI within the context of connected supply chain processes, so a signal in one area can inform what happens next.


[Microsoft offers one example of what connected, data-driven planning can achieve](https://www.sap.com/asset/dynamic/2024/01/2c9c4f28-a57e-0010-bca6-c68f7e60039b.html) . Using SAP supply chain planning solutions, the company reduced manual planning processes by 50%, helping its teams minimize inventory and supply chain risk while creating more time to focus on higher-value decisions.


Illumina, a global genomics and human health company, provides another example. Using[SAP Integrated Business Planning](https://www.sap.com/products/scm/integrated-business-planning.html) , Illumina achieved a 40% reduction in excess inventory. The company is also applying AI across its supply chain operations as it continues its transformation toward more intelligent planning.[Learn more in this ASUG Talks interview.](https://www.asug.com/insights/how-illumina-leveraged-sap-integrated-business-planning-ibp-to-drive-a-40-reduction-in-excess-inventory)


To hear from more customers about how they see AI changing supply chain planning, watch[Supply Chain Planning, Reimagined for the Agentic Era](https://www.sap.com/videos/1349696) .


This is also central to how we think about[Autonomous Supply Chain Management at SAP](https://www.sap.com/products/scm.html) . Decision velocity matters, but speed alone is not the objective. Companies need to recognize change, understand its implications, and coordinate the right response based on relevant business context.


## **Connecting planning to action**


Planning becomes more valuable when companies can act on it. With[SAP Integrated Business Planning](https://www.sap.com/products/scm/integrated-business-planning.html) , companies can connect strategic, tactical, and operational planning across demand, supply, inventory, and response. Those decisions can then connect with processes across manufacturing, warehousing, transportation, business networks, and the broader enterprise.


This reflects a larger shift toward supply chain orchestration.[As I have written previously](https://news.sap.com/2026/06/reimagining-supply-chain-strategic-vision-into-operational-reality/) , organizations have made significant progress within individual functions, but the opportunity is to connect planning, procurement, manufacturing, logistics, and other processes into a more coordinated operating model.


A planning decision may change a production schedule, affecting material availability, warehouse capacity, transportation, and, ultimately, customer commitments. Connecting these processes helps companies understand those downstream impacts and make informed trade-offs based on what is best for the broader supply chain and the business, rather than optimizing one function in isolation.


The latest IDC MarketScape results extend beyond planning as well. SAP has also been named a Leader in IDC MarketScape 2026 Warehouse Management assessments for Manufacturing‡ and Retail‡‡. While these are separate assessments, we believe the recognition across[planning](https://www.sap.com/products/scm/supply-chain-planning.html) and[warehouse management](https://www.sap.com/products/scm/extended-warehouse-management.html) underscores the importance of connecting decisions across the supply chain. To learn more, read[SAP Named a Leader in Two 2026 IDC MarketScapes: Worldwide Warehouse Management for Manufacturing and for Retail](https://news.sap.com/2026/11/sap-leader-idc-marketscapes-warehouse-management-manufacturing-retail/) .


## **From connected planning to greater autonomy**


AI is accelerating this shift.[At SAP Connect, we introduced new capabilities](https://news.sap.com/2026/10/joule-assistants-agents-advance-autonomous-scm/) across Joule Assistants and specialized Joule Agents designed to help supply chain teams sense, analyze, and act across connected processes. The Supply Chain Planning Assistant, for example, is designed to help planners sense, simulate, and resolve exceptions while understanding downstream impacts.


This is where we see Autonomous Supply Chain Management becoming practical. The goal is not autonomy for autonomy’s sake. It is to help people spend less time coordinating routine work and resolving exceptions and more time making the decisions that strengthen the business.


As AI plays a larger role, trust remains essential. Leaders need the ability to understand decisions, establish guardrails, and maintain accountability. Agentic AI should strengthen human decision-making, giving people the context and intelligence to act with greater confidence while keeping them firmly in control of the decisions that matter most.


## **Turning recognition into customer value**


We are proud of this recognition from IDC MarketScape, but the real measure of progress is what our customers can accomplish.


Our focus is helping supply chain leaders connect planning and execution, build greater agility into their operations, and make informed decisions faster. Increasingly, that means bringing together applications, data, and AI so organizations can move from insight to action across the supply chain.


We believe these latest IDC MarketScape results are an important acknowledgment of that direction. More importantly, we believe they reinforce the path we are pursuing with our customers toward more connected, intelligent, and autonomous supply chains.


Learn more about[SAP supply chain planning solutions](https://www.sap.com/products/scm/supply-chain-planning.html) .


---


Hagen Heubach is chief marketing officer for SAP Supply Chain Management.
